label: ExtremeSwitching X465-48P
description: ExtremeSwitching X465-48P - 48x 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ-45 with 802.3at 30 W PoE+ on every port, MACsec capable, one empty VIM5 uplink slot, two 40G dedicated stacking ports (unpopulated), rear RJ-45 console and a 1G out-of-band management port; 364 Gbps aggregated switch bandwidth, 270.8 Mpps.

fabric.note: Extreme states 364 aggregated switch bandwidth and 270.8 frame forwarding rate for the X465-48P (datasheet Performance and Scale table, https://extr-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/df5d3e48f1834936bc0d1caeae677c02?v=f38c16b6). The vendor figure counts the VIM5 uplink capacity and the two 40G stacking ports as well as the front panel, so it is larger than the aggregate of the Ethernet ports modelled here; nothing on the modelled ports is capped by it.

notes: Port census: 48 x 10/100/1000BASE-T 802.3at (30 W) MACsec-capable access ports, ports 1:1-1:48. The 48P is the only 1G member whose port row states 802.3at rather than 802.3bt, so 802.3bt is not declared here. The field behaviour still powers 802.3af PDs, but the datasheet port row and the family standards table name only 802.3at, so af is not declared either. VIM5 slot empty: VIM5-4X (4x 1/10G SFP+), VIM5-4XE (4x 1/10G SFP+, LRM/MACsec), VIM5-4Y / VIM5-4YE (4x 10/25G SFP28), VIM5-2Y (2x 25G SFP28), VIM5-2Q (2x 40G QSFP+). The module is not hot-swappable and its ports are not modelled here, so the box is the bare chassis. S1 and S2 are 2x 40G QSFP+ stacking ports on the front panel, 42 Gbps per link under SummitStack-V160; the stacking-support option is always enabled on the X465 and these are native stacking-only ports, so they are not modelled as Ethernet data ports. Console is the rear-panel RJ-45 serial port (plus a USB micro-B console that takes priority when connected), and the rear also carries a 10/100/1000BASE-T out-of-band management port, modelled as mgmt. Dual-core 1.5 GHz x86, 2 GB DDR4, 8 GB eMMC, 3 fan modules, system power 255 W. Idle 82 W, maximum 1747 W with every port at 30 W. Sources: https://extr-p-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/df5d3e48f1834936bc0d1caeae677c02?v=f38c16b6, https://cdn.blueally.com/netsolutionstore/datasheets/switches/x465-series-data-sheet.pdf, https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Wired_Hardware/ExtremeSwitching_Installation_Guide_for_Switches_Using_ExtremeXOS_Version_30/topics/extremeswitching_x465_series_switches_technical_specifications.shtml, https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Wired_Hardware/ExtremeSwitching_Installation_Guide_for_Switches_Using_ExtremeXOS_Version_30/topics/extremeswitching_x465_series_switches.shtml, https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Universal_Hardware/Universal_Hardware_Common/topics/build_stacks/extremeswitching_x465_stacking.shtml.

poe.note: 1440 W with two 1100 W PSUs or one/two 2000 W PSUs, exactly 48 x 30 W, so the 30 W class is available on every port at once; a single 1100 W unit gives 845 W and a single 715 W unit 460 W (https://documentation.extremenetworks.com/ExtremeSwitching%20Installation%20Guide%20for%20Switches%20Using%20ExtremeXOS%20Version%2030/Wired_Hardware/ExtremeSwitching_Installation_Guide_for_Switches_Using_ExtremeXOS_Version_30/topics/extremeswitching_x465_series_switches_technical_specifications.shtml). This is the 802.3at Type 2 member of the family, not a bt box.
